details:
Q1: How should the facts helper handle references to repositories other than the current one?
Choices:
A. Stop reading other repositories. Only the current repository (`--repo`) is queried. `--consumer-repos-file` is still accepted so existing callers keep working, but it has no effect. A reference to another repository gets one line saying it was "not read (cross-repository)". No extra API calls. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Keep reading listed consumer repositories, but only show facts for public ones. Add `isPrivate` to the existing single GraphQL query and `repository.private` from the run response, and leave out private non-current repositories. No extra API calls, but this still uses the shared PAT for those reads.
C. Check each referenced repository against the issue author's identity first: call `repos/{slug}/collaborators/{login}/permission` once per repository and leave the repository out on any failure. **Note:** this adds one REST call per repository and still exposes facts to readers of the current repo who lack access to the referenced repo. Combined with Q2:A it would also need the PAT, which defeats Q2:A.
Q2: Which credential should the "Fetch GitHub facts for the questions" step use?
Choices:
A. Keep `secrets.GH_PAT` for this step, now limited to the current repository by Q1. PR-merge and run facts keep working in every consumer without changing any wrapper's `permissions:`. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Switch to the repository-scoped `github.token`, so reads of other repositories are impossible by design. Add `pull-requests: read` and `actions: read` to `internal-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml` and `workflow-templates/ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml`. Until consumers pick up the synced wrapper, PR and run facts fail open (they show as "could not be read"). **Note:** incompatible with Q1:B and Q1:C, which need cross-repository reads.
